programs.title: Chernobyl: Inside the Meltdown
programs.desc:
On April 26, 1986, an explosion destroyed the fourth block of the Chernobyl power plant.The accident was caused by design defects in the reactor and errors during the safety test.It was the worst nuclear disaster in history.The explosion released 400 times more radiation than the bomb dropped on Hiroshima.40 years after the tragedy, its consequences will be shown - from KGB activities to military operations in Ukraine.There will be plenty of witness accounts that will shed new light on the dramatic events.The speakers will include:liquidator working on the roof of reactor 3 and journalist Wyatt Andrews, who was covering the information blockade in Moscow
On April 28, the remains of the fourth reactor were still unextinguished.The authorities finally decide to evacuate.50,000 people take supplies for three days.They don't know that they will never return to their homes.Meanwhile, firefighters with burns are being watched by the KGB.Swedish technicians at the Forsmark nuclear power plant are the first to detect increased levels of radiation.They alert the world about the catastrophe that the USSR authorities are trying to hide.Events two weeks after the explosion will be discussed.The authors will explain how attempts were made to hide the truth.

programs.title: Air Crash Investigation 21
programs.desc: Reconstructions of real plane crashes.By recreating the course of events, the program's creators try to understand what led to the unfortunate events.They recreate the circumstances in which the tragedy occurred: the weather, the atmosphere on board the plane, the decisions and actions of the pilots.They also show the work of people investigating the causes of disasters and conduct a computer flight simulation.Viewers can hear various comments from specialists and testimonies of witnesses to these events.The creators of the program will prove that air accidents are often caused by human slowness and lack of imagination.Each disaster is thoroughly analyzed and the lessons learned help minimize the number of tragedies in the future.
